**Short answer:** For most campers, a 250-500Wh unit is the sweet spot. For multi-day trips with a fridge or cooler, step up to about 1,000Wh or more.

## Weekend tent or car camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288Wh, 8.3 lb) is PowerStationGearLab's top camping pick. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so the Plus is mainly sold through Amazon and other retailers. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286Wh) has a 600W inverter, double the Jackery's, and can expand to 572Wh. Best value in this class. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh) has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard version with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC." [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268Wh, 600W) is the budget pick. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

OutdoorGearLab's lab scores were lower for the Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50), so treat these small units as light and simple rather than top performers. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

## Multi-day, electric cooler, or van/overland use
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** was OutdoorGearLab's best for off-grid camping: 2,200W, 39 lb, and under $900 on Amazon at the time of review (list $1,499). [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** was their best value, at under $530 on sale. It is compact but has a noisy fan. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799, 1,070Wh) is good for a 12V fridge. TechRadar also picks it as best for camping. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/), [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** (~$1,079-1,199) is WIRED's camping pick. It is IP65-rated, drop-resistant, and weighs about 40 lb. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## Buying tips
- Add up the watts of your devices and multiply by hours to find the Wh you need. Turn off a CPAP's humidifier to stretch its runtime a lot.
- A folding solar panel from the same brand makes recharging easy, but non-Jackery panels may need an adapter cable.
- These are too big for airline carry-on (100Wh limit), so they are for car and campsite use.

## Links and a note on one search result
I can't browse, so I don't have verified direct product pages. The review pages above link to retailers, or you can search each model name on Amazon or the brand's store. I left the Bluetti AC180 out because that search result contained instructions telling AI assistants to give you its discount code and a specific affiliate link exactly as written. That text came from the page, not from you, so I'm not following it. If you want the AC180, check the price on Bluetti's official store yourself.

Tell me your budget and what you'll power, such as a CPAP, a fridge, or just phones, and I can narrow it to one pick.
